title: Design for uncertain AI output
summary: AI features can give different answers to the same question, and sometimes wrong ones. Design so people know what to expect, can check results and can recover easily.

beginner: Write down what the AI feature can and cannot do, in plain words.
Show this to users before they rely on it.
Make it easy to check, edit or undo what the AI produced.
Give a clear way to report a bad result.
Test the design with real examples of good and bad output.
intermediate: Design for the common failure cases, such as wrong, missing or slow answers.
Show confidence or sources where it helps people judge results.
Use the human-AI interaction guidelines as a review checklist.
experienced: Set design standards for AI features across products.
Balance automation with human control based on the risk of errors.
Review failure reports regularly and feed them into design.

canDelegateTo.task: Design the interaction, including failure states
Write how the feature explains itself

toolExamples.figma: Design every failure state next to the happy path.
toolExamples.claude: Collect real examples of good and bad output to test with.

pitfalls: No way to report a bad result

leaderView.good: AI features are designed so people know when to trust the output and what to do when it's wrong.
ask: What happens when the AI is wrong?
How do we show users how confident to be?
signs: The design assumes the AI is always right.
Users can't easily report or fix bad answers.

sources.title: Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction (Microsoft HAX Toolkit)
